prompt: Main session (Fable) — wrap-up. Run as the orchestrator following dev-lead's playbook, because cloud sessions cap agent nesting at one level (Agents handbook, build-round rule 6). Steps taken: product-manager spec → researcher + ui-designer in parallel → builder A (calculation core + tests) and builder B (page + build script) in parallel against one pinned contract → verifier → code-reviewer → fix round 2 to the same two builders → verifier round 2.
report:
Verdict: SHIP. 10 dispatches, 2 rounds. What happened along the way, honestly:
- The researcher's worked example under-counted blocks because its room list covered half the floor; the orchestrator added a "list every space" rule (assumptions.md §7) before the builders started.
- Verifier round 1 failed step 3 because the orchestrator wrote a log record after committing the generated page — a sequencing mistake, not a code bug. The verifier misdiagnosed it as the build script logging runs; corrected in the record.
- Code review found two golden-rule violations: 13 editable assumptions that didn't affect the maths (the page claimed they did), and ground-slab steel with no named assumption. Both fixed in round 2, and a test now sweeps every assumption to prove it either moves the result or is marked reference-only.
- Final: 25 tests green, build idempotent, browser smoke green at 1440 and 390. Sample house: 8,053 blocks, 129.1 m³ concrete, 12.0 t steel, ≈9,058 OMR at the default (editable, unsourced-for-Oman) prices.
Left for the owner: prices marked "Guessing" need a real supplier quote before anyone relies on the OMR total; floorplan upload and Arabic are v2.
